claims.text: Real-time adaptive laser-power modulation will improve dimensional precision relative to constant-power additive manufacturing.
Real-time adaptive laser-power modulation will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Real-time adaptive laser-power modulation will reduce fabrication-induced defects, including porosity.
As-fabricated AlCoCrFeNi or similar components made at constant laser power exhibit dimensional deviations, residual stresses, and porosity.
The proposed controller modulates laser power in real time using in-situ temperature and melt-pool measurements.
Adaptive laser-power modulation will produce a more uniform and controlled melt pool.
Adaptive laser-power modulation will decrease peak temperatures and thermal gradients.
Lower peak temperatures and thermal gradients will refine the microstructure, reduce porosity, and improve grain homogeneity.
Adaptive modulation minimizes thermal overshoots and rapid cooling during deposition.
Minimizing thermal overshoots and rapid cooling reduces residual stress and inhibits defect nucleation.
A more uniform microstructure and improved interlayer bonding enhance dimensional accuracy and mechanical properties.
Adaptive control will increase yield strength and ductility relative to fixed laser parameters.
Constant laser power and a fixed scanning path produce inconsistent melt-pool dynamics, higher defect concentrations, and dimensional inaccuracies.
The proposed benefit should hold under typical DED or laser powder-bed-fusion conditions for alloys similar to AlCoCrFeNi.
Laser power, scanning speed, and powder-feed rate are coupled to AlCoCrFeNi laser-cladding quality metrics such as microhardness, dilution rate, and aspect ratio.

Machine-learning-based process-condition optimization produced greater than 98% relative density in laser powder-bed-fusion products and was validated using Fe60Co15Ni15Cr10 medium-entropy-alloy powder.
